custom_fields.label: Employees may clock themselves in
custom_fields.description: Everyone who does needs a login. An employee with no User has no session, so there is nothing to check and no permission to write under.

custom_fields.label: Close an open day at the shift's end
custom_fields.description: A forgotten clock-out is the commonest cause of a wrong half day. The closed log is marked as automatic rather than left looking real.

custom_fields.label: Ask why on the way out
custom_fields.description: Break, lunch, errand, done for the day. It makes a day of gaps readable.

custom_fields.label: A passkey on their own phone
custom_fields.description: Who. One credential per employee; a second needs a reset here.

custom_fields.label: No passkey refuses the clock-in
custom_fields.description: Off, a missing passkey is only flagged. Turn it off in a workspace that cannot reset a lost phone the same morning.

custom_fields.label: The network they arrived on
custom_fields.description: The address the request came from, against the places below. A browser cannot read a wifi name and never will.

custom_fields.label: Where the browser says they are
custom_fields.description: Needs HRMS's own geolocation tracking switched on above, and the employee's permission once.

custom_fields.label: Network and place
custom_fields.description: Either is the sensible default: they prove the same thing two ways, and demanding both means one poor GPS fix stops somebody working.

custom_fields.label: Refuse below
custom_fields.description: Confidence out of a hundred. Below this the clock-in is refused and the reason is shown.

custom_fields.label: Flag below
custom_fields.description: Between the two the clock-in is written and goes in the review queue.

custom_fields.label: Ask for a photo
custom_fields.description: A live frame from the camera, never a file. It says who pressed the button; it cannot say where, because there is no location in a photo.

custom_fields.label: What the system may learn
custom_fields.description: Only clock-ins already corroborated another way may teach it anything, so three people in a café cannot promote the café. Nothing learned ever widens who may clock in, only where.

custom_fields.label: Learn a new office address
custom_fields.description: A router reboot or a second line stops locking everybody out on a Monday.

custom_fields.label: Learn where people actually stand
custom_fields.description: A warehouse gate two hundred metres from the registered door becomes a second circle, never a wider one.

custom_fields.label: Learn home networks and home zones
custom_fields.description: For remote workers. Off by default because plenty of workplaces would rather not hold somebody's home address.

custom_fields.label: Proposals need
custom_fields.description: How many different people, and how many clock-ins, before a proposal is confirmed on its own.
